record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a directed planar graph G together with k ordered pairs of vertices (r1, s1), ..., (rk, sk), is there a fixed-parameter algorithm in k that decides whether G contains k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths P1, ..., Pk such that Pi runs from ri to si for every i?

evidence.quote: Question: Does G have k vertex-disjoint paths P1,...,Pk with Pi running from ri to si?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a directed planar graph and let (r_1, s_1), ..., (r_k, s_k) be k ordered pairs of vertices of G. A solution to the k-Disjoint Directed Paths instance (G, (r_1,s_1), ..., (r_k,s_k)) is a collection of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint directed paths P_1, ..., P_k in G such that, for each i ∈ {1,...,k}, P_i is directed from r_i to s_i.

Does there exist an algorithm that, given (G, (r_1,s_1), ..., (r_k,s_k)) as input, decides whether such a solution exists and runs in time f(k) · |V(G)|^{O(1)} for some computable function f depending only on k? In other words, is the Directed Planar Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the number k of terminal pairs?
artifact.status_search_result: Cygan, Marx, Pilipczuk, and Pilipczuk (FOCS 2013, arXiv:1304.4207) proved that the planar directed k-Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem is fixed-parameter tractable, with running time 2^{2^{O(k^2)}} · n^{O(1)}. This resolves the question in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: The planar directed k-Vertex-Disjoint Paths problem is fixed-parameter tractable
status_evidence.snippet: Cygan, Marx, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk give an algorithm with running time 2^{2^{O(k^2)}} n^{O(1)} showing fixed-parameter tractability.
status_evidence.claim: The planar directed k-vertex-disjoint paths problem is FPT in k.

status_evidence.title: The Planar Directed K-Vertex-Disjoint Paths Problem Is Fixed-Parameter Tractable (FOCS 2013)
status_evidence.snippet: FOCS 2013, pp. 197–206. Resolves the long-standing open question that the problem is FPT on planar digraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Published proof that the problem is fixed-parameter tractable.
